correctness.rationale: For every selected recovery pair, binary local distance \(2\) forces the two coordinate functions to be equal or complementary on the whole code. This gives equivalence classes of size at least \(2\) and an injective weighted quotient. With length \(9\) there are at most four classes; the only four-class weight pattern is \((2,2,2,3)\), and each fixed value of the weight-\(3\) coordinate leaves a length-three binary code of minimum distance at least \(2\), hence at most four words. The explicit eight-word code attains the bound. The packaged verifier independently checks the witness and exhausts all reduced partitions and subsets.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact finite invariant singled out by a September 2026 benchmark table. The result closes the published nonlinear gap from \(8\le M_{\max}\le64/5\) to equality at \(8\), showing that nonlinear codes provide no size gain in a binary locality-one row where the new three-block LP is still nonintegral. The proof also exposes a structural reduction from arbitrary overlapping recovery pairs to a weighted quotient, which is reusable beyond the single computation.
